description.p: Screenator is a vibe-coded screen annotation tool for X11. It is based on Gromit-MPX 1.4.2.

Draw over any running application with a pen, arrow, text, shapes or eraser, change line colour, thickness and opacity, choose the text font and shape fill from the floating icon or the tray menu, and keep the annotations on screen for as long as you need them.

ul.li: Floating icon.A small draggable icon opens the tool and settings menu.
Hotkey-based.Toggle painting, clear the screen, toggle visibility or quit from the keyboard.
Tray menu.The same menu is available from the system tray.
Configurable.Line colour, thickness, opacity, text font, shape fill and floating icon size are remembered across restarts.

description.p: Removes the inherited Gromit-MPX global shortcuts. F9 is now a single global shortcut that shows or hides the floating icon at any time, while Shift+F9, Ctrl+F9, Alt+F9, F8 and Shift+F8 are no longer grabbed. Show Floating Icon moves directly below Toggle Visibility in the menu and is labelled with F9. Ctrl+F is removed from the screen paper shortcuts; Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z and Alt+F4 remain.

Redesigns the stylus first side button: a short press steps through the selected Color or Thickness, and a long press activates the eraser for as long as it is held, including while hovering. The Button 1 Mode menu now lists only Color and Thickness. The per-tool messages are replaced by one colourful hints dialog shown at startup, with Show Hints below Toggle Visibility and a remembered Never show hints again option. With the Eraser tool selected, the mouse wheel changes the eraser size.

Adds full stylus support. The tip draws like the left mouse button with pressure ignored, the first side button offers Eraser, Color and Thickness modes, a short click of the second side button acts like Escape/right click, and a long press opens the Button 1 Mode menu. A help message appears once when a stylus is detected. Line Thickness now includes 4 px and 5 px, and the settings indicator has nine thickness sectors. Includes the changes since 4.0: the Random Signal tool, Parallel Lines arrowheads, the Arrow tool heads handle, undoable Clear Screen, and Escape finishing or exiting the current tool.

Adds a heads handle to the Arrow tool: press it to reset the arrowheads to none, then drag in any direction to cycle start, end and both. New arrows still default to the traditional single head at the end. Clearing the screen can now be undone from the Undo menu, and Redo clears it again.

Adds a Random Signal tool to the Shapes submenu. A click places a default-size signal and dragging sizes it; a handle outside the left edge sets the smoothness from 1 (sharpest) to 16 (smoothest), and clicking the signal rolls a new one. The waveform is centred on its mean, uses 60% of the frame height, and is smoothed with a Gaussian filter and a smooth cubic curve. The Parallel Lines tool now has a handle outside the right edge for arrowheads on the top, bottom or both ends, with sharp heads placed at the line tips. While painting, Escape finishes the current shape or exits the tool, the same as a right click.

Adds a settings indicator ring around the floating icon: the inner ring shows the line thickness as magenta sectors (one per thickness), and the outer six pixel ring shows the line colour and the shape fill colour, or twelve black and white stripes when shapes are not filled. Line Color and Shapes Fill Color have a Custom... entry that opens a colour chooser, starts at magenta and is remembered; the mouse wheel includes the custom colour. Tool hints now start with the tool name, and right-to-left text is previewed and its caret placed correctly. The About dialog is a fresh, simple borderless window that no longer leaves the desktop panel unresponsive after it is closed. Includes the changes since 3.0: the Settings submenu with Save annotations on exit, rect(x) in the Math Function presets, screen-paper shortcuts and their message, four corner resize handles for editable shapes, and math plots scaled to fill their frames.

Redesigns the settings indicator as a ring around the floating icon. The inner white ring is divided into seven sectors, one for each line thickness, and the sectors up to the selected thickness are filled light orange; every sector has a one pixel black stroke. The outer six pixel ring shows the line colour in its upper half and the shape fill colour in its lower half, or twelve black and white radial stripes when shapes are not filled. Left or right clicking the ring opens the same menu as the floating icon. The first text caret is now drawn at the centred editor position from the first frame, so it no longer leaves a static line below the blinking caret.

Adds shortcuts that work while a screen paper is active: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo, Alt+F4 quits, Ctrl+F shows or hides the floating icon and Ctrl+T shows or hides the drawings. A one-time message explains them when a paper is turned on and can be switched off with "Never show this message again". Ctrl+T and Toggle Visibility now keep the paper visible and hide only the drawings, and the message is only shown when switching from None to a paper. Math plots are scaled to the curve's real minimum and maximum, so positive functions and delta spikes fill the frame and the bottom of the graph sits on the bottom handles. The first text caret no longer appears in the top-left corner before the text editor is placed.

Adds a Settings submenu with Save annotations on exit, Change Font, Show Floating Icon, Show Settings Indicator and Reset Settings. With Save annotations on exit on (the default), the drawings are saved to ~/.config/screenator-annotations.png when Screenator quits and restored on the next start; Clear Screen removes the saved drawing. Adds rect(x), a rectangle pulse that is 1 for |x| <= 1/2 and 0 elsewhere, to the Math Function presets and functions. The settings indicator now takes input, so clicks and scrolling on it no longer reach the desktop or the application below. Editable shapes now have four square size handles, one on each corner, and dragging a corner resizes the shape with the opposite corner fixed; the text tool scales its font from the corner drag.

Keeps the drawings and the screen paper visible while a dialog is open. The Math Function settings, the tool hints, the About dialog and the font chooser are now shown above the full-screen annotation window instead of hiding it, are centred, and take the keyboard focus directly. Clicks outside a dialog no longer paint on the paper, and the global hotkeys stay with the dialog while it is open. The dialogs have no window-manager title bar and are closed with their own buttons.

Adds editable handles to the text, ellipse and rounded rectangle tools: every placed shape keeps a square size handle, a round rotation handle and can be moved by dragging inside it (holding Ctrl snaps the rotation to 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 and so on). The line and arrow tools stay editable too, with a handle on each end point, and their direction snaps to the same angles while Ctrl is held. Snapping applies only with Ctrl, and the tools that snap show a hint about it that can be switched off. The triangle snaps the angle at a dragged vertex to 30, 45, 60 or 90 degrees, and the polygon inner-radius handle snaps to the flat edge. Adds a Math Function tool with Rectangular y = f(x) and Polar r = f(theta) modes (theta is reserved for the angle and defaults to a full circle from 0 to 2*pi; pi and e are the constants, the rectangular default is cos(2*pi*x) from -2 to 2, and a removable hole such as sin(x)/x at x = 0 is filled in with its limit) and plots it inside a resizable and rotatable frame. The Math dialog also has a preset drop-down (cos(2*pi*x), sin(2*pi*x), unit step, Dirac delta, e^(x), log(x), 1/x and sin(x)/x, with theta in place of x in polar mode), and a delta is drawn as an arrow where its argument is zero. Adds 1 px and 2 px to the line thickness menu and a Parallel Lines tool that draws 2 to 40 evenly spaced vertical lines with the current line thickness, with a handle that sets their number. The rectangle, angled line and angled arrow tools were removed; the rounded rectangle covers sharp rectangles. Adds Screen Paper (Plain, Ruled and Graph) that turns the screen into paper and keeps the mouse and keyboard from reaching the applications below, a redesigned settings indicator next to the floating icon, and a Show Floating Icon option. Selecting a tool shows a hint that describes that tool's mouse buttons, mouse wheel and handles, and each tool's hint has its own "Never show this message again" option. The mouse wheel changes the line colour, the bucket fill colour or the eraser size depending on the tool, Orange and Gray were added to the line and fill colours, and the bucket erases the enclosed fill when None is selected.

Adds a paint bucket to the Shapes menu that fills enclosed areas with the shape fill colour, a node-based Bezier spline tool with editable symmetric handles (hold Ctrl to move one side only), a polygon tool with handles for its sides, radius, rotation and inner radius, a triangle tool with a handle on each vertex, a roundness handle for the rounded rectangle, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo while painting, a 120 px eraser size, and an About dialog that credits the author. Green is now the first shape fill colour and the default fill. Selecting a tool shows a short hint about the mouse buttons, and the Spline hint explains how to move its handles; both hints can be switched off and are kept when the settings are reset.

First release. Fork of Gromit-MPX 1.4.2 with a floating icon menu, tray menu, configurable pen settings, a translucent marker, a text tool with a selectable font, free and angled line and arrow tools, shape tools with an optional fill colour, an adjustable eraser, and a reset option.
